events.event_title: US-China Tariff Escalation & Trade War Reignition
events.event_description: The Trump administration has reimposed aggressive tariffs on Chinese goods (up to 145%), with China retaliating at 125%. This creates immediate supply chain disruption pressure on importers and reshuffles manufacturing beneficiaries. A near-term catalyst exists around any negotiation signals or further escalation announcements.
events.rationale: GFF (Griffon Corp) manufactures doors/building products with US-based operations that benefit from import substitution. POWL (Powell Industries) is a domestic electrical equipment maker gaining from reshoring. CEVA (semiconductor IP) has China revenue exposure making it a bearish play. PRCT (Procept BioRobotics) has supply chain exposure to Asian components. These mid-caps have more direct binary exposure than mega-caps already priced in.

tickers.entry_trigger: GFF breaks above $96.50 on tariff escalation news OR closes above 20-day MA ($95.40) with volume confirmation; avoid chasing above $98
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $92.80 (breaks 50-day support) OR tariff truce announced; take 60% profit at $100 if reached within 3 weeks
tickers.risk: RSI at 64.4 shows overbought conditions—vulnerable to profit-taking pullback before tariff catalyst fully prices in; mega-cap competitors already positioned; tariff deal negotiation could deflate thesis within days

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $305 on tariff escalation news OR pullback to $290-295 support on negotiation rumors with volume confirmation
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $285 (thesis break) OR take profits at $320+ if tariff narrative reverses within 3 weeks
tickers.risk: Tariff deal/de-escalation announcement collapses thesis immediately; POWL's electrical equipment demand tied to capex cycles which may lag; valuation already reflects some reshoring premium at $299; execution risk on domestic manufacturing ramp

events.event_title: Defense Spending Surge — NATO & European Rearmament
events.event_description: European NATO members are rapidly expanding defense budgets toward and beyond 2% GDP targets, with Germany alone committing €100B+ to its military. The US DoD budget remains elevated. Near-term catalyst: defense contract awards, earnings beats from smaller defense primes, and potential supplemental spending bills.
events.rationale: KTOS (Kratos Defense) specializes in drone systems and hypersonic targets — direct beneficiary of next-gen warfare spending. DRS (Leonardo DRS) is a mid-cap defense electronics firm with growing DoD contracts. CACI International provides defense IT/intel services with recurring government revenue. VEC (Vectrus, now V2X) handles military base logistics and overseas operations. These are less saturated than LMT/RTX but have direct program exposure.

tickers.entry_trigger: AXON closes above $435 on volume >2M shares, or breaks above recent consolidation on defense contract announcement news
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $420 on high volume, or exit at 10-week mark if target not approached; take 50% off at $450
tickers.risk: AXON's primary revenue (body cameras, cloud software, AI analytics for law enforcement) has minimal direct NATO/DoD exposure; defense spending surge benefits KTOS, DRS, CACI more directly. AXON may underperform thesis if contracts don't materialize quickly.

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $58.50 on volume >2M shares, or pullback to $54–$55 range with RSI <40 + positive defense contract news
tickers.exit_condition: Exit 50% at $65–$66; trail stop at $56.50 for remainder. Close all if RSI >70 without new catalyst or on earnings miss
tickers.risk: KTOS is micro-cap (~$1.2B market cap) with volatile swings; execution risk on hypersonic/drone contracts; potential profit-taking after 15%+ run; competition from RTX/LMT; geopolitical de-escalation reduces urgency

events.event_title: AI Infrastructure Buildout — Power Grid & Data Center Bottleneck
events.event_description: Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon) have committed $300B+ in 2025 capex, almost entirely toward AI data centers. The binding constraint is now power — grid interconnection queues, transformer shortages, and cooling solutions. Utility commission approvals and transformer delivery timelines are imminent catalysts.
events.rationale: NPWR (NET Power) is developing natural gas power with carbon capture targeted at data centers — speculative but high-beta catalyst play. POWL (Powell Industries) makes switchgear critical for data center power distribution and is seeing order backlogs. GEV (GE Vernova) is the pure-play grid equipment and gas turbine name with direct data center utility exposure. SMDI (Standard Motor — less relevant) — substitute NVEE (NV5 Global), an engineering firm winning data center site and grid consulting contracts. These are mid-caps with direct order flow tied to the buildout.

tickers.entry_trigger: Utility commission approval announcement for data center power interconnection (next 4-8 weeks) + RSI break above 50 on volume; alternatively, order backlog disclosure from Powell or GE Vernova confirming data center transformer/switchgear acceleration
tickers.exit_condition: Take 40% at +60% gain (~$2.80); trail stop at 8% below swing high after breakout; exit full position if utility approval delays into Q2 2025 or if broader capex guidance from hyperscalers softens
tickers.risk: NPWR is pre-revenue/speculative carbon capture play—execution risk is extreme; power grid approvals are political and subject to indefinite delay; transformer supply chain may ease faster than priced in; compete with cheaper diesel/grid alternatives; macro rate shock crushes capex cycle; broader AI hype deflation

tickers.entry_trigger: Break above $305 on volume >500K shares, or pullback to $290-295 on confirmation of Q1 2025 data center order guidance in earnings
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $285 (thesis break), or take profits at $330-335 on utility commission delays >6 months or competitive switchgear capacity relief
tickers.risk: Transformer supply constraints may ease faster than expected; hyperscaler power capex could shift to alternative grid solutions (distributed solar, batteries); POWL order backlog conversion execution risk; valuation already reflects some infrastructure narrative at RSI 56.7

tickers.entry_trigger: GEV breaks above $165 on volume (52-week high confirmation) following utility commission approval announcements for major data center interconnects, or on earnings beat with FY2025 power equipment order guidance >15% YoY
tickers.exit_condition: Exit 50% at $180 on first major utility approval catalyst; exit remaining 50% on break below $155 or if data center capex guidance downgrades materially (>10% reduction), or 10-week hold maximum
tickers.risk: Utility commission delays push catalysts beyond 12-week window; transformer lead times already extended but may not translate to orders; GEV valuation already reflects some buildout expectations (P/E premium justified only if execution flawless); grid infrastructure momentum is real but competitive (POWL, EATON) already trading on this thesis

events.event_title: GLP-1 Drug Obesity Market Expansion & Supply Normalization
events.event_description: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly continue expanding GLP-1 production capacity. FDA decisions on new indications (heart failure, sleep apnea approvals already hit), oral formulations, and biosimilar timelines create near-term catalysts. The second-order impact hits medical device, food, and specialty pharma sectors meaningfully.
events.rationale: TNDM (Tandem Diabetes Care) faces bearish pressure as GLP-1 drugs reduce insulin-dependent diabetes cases, threatening their insulin pump market long-term. CELH (Celsius Holdings) faces mixed pressure as GLP-1 users reduce caloric intake, affecting energy drink consumption. ITCI (Intra-Cellular Therapies) is a CNS-focused pharma that could benefit as metabolic-CNS combo therapies gain attention. SDGR (Schrödinger) provides AI drug discovery platforms being used by GLP-1 competitors to accelerate next-gen molecules — indirect but real beneficiary. These are less obvious than NVO/LLY themselves.

tickers.entry_trigger: NVCR breaks above $18.50 on volume >2M shares OR FDA approval announcement for new TTFields indication (CNS/metabolic); confirm RSI <70 at entry
tickers.exit_condition: Close below $17.00 on volume spike OR RSI >75 without follow-through; take profits at $20.50 if reached within 4 weeks
tickers.risk: NVCR is oncology-focused (glioblastoma); GLP-1 impact is indirect/speculative. Real catalyst dependency is weak—stock moves on trial data, not obesity market. FDA disappointment on new indications could trigger sharp reversal. Low beta to stated event theme.

tickers.entry_trigger: TNDM breaks below $16.00 on volume >2M shares OR FDA announces new GLP-1 indication + simultaneous Novo/Lilly capacity expansion press release
tickers.exit_condition: RSI drops below 35 (oversold capitulation) OR TNDM announces partnerships/pivots into GLP-1 management devices OR hold >4 weeks without additional GLP-1 headwinds—exit at 15% loss
tickers.risk: GLP-1 adoption rate slower than consensus; TNDM's pump innovation/pediatric market resilience underestimated; short squeeze on heavily shorted stock; regulatory approval delays reduce near-term catalyst velocity
